sections.title: Level 2 Concept Overview
sections.content: Level 2 seating arrangement involves double rows, mixed circular arrangements, square or rectangular structures, and one additional variable like color or fruit preference. Students must manage multiple clues and sometimes maintain more than one possible case before eliminating the wrong one.

sections.title: Double Row Arrangement (8–10 Persons)
sections.content: In double row arrangements, two parallel rows face each other. If one row faces North, the opposite row faces South. Persons sitting directly opposite are in the same column. Step 1: Draw two parallel rows. Step 2: Mark facing direction clearly. Step 3: Place definite clues first. Step 4: Check opposite positions carefully.

sections.title: Mixed Circular Arrangement (Some Facing Center, Some Outside)
sections.content: In mixed circular arrangement, some persons face the center and some face outside. For center-facing persons, left and right are reversed from your perspective. For outside-facing persons, left and right are normal. Always mark C (center) or O (outside) beside each name before applying clues.

sections.title: Square or Rectangular Arrangement
sections.content: In square or rectangular seating, people may sit at corners and middle of sides. Corner persons usually have only two neighbors, while middle-side persons may have three. Step 1: Mark corners first. Step 2: Fill side-middle positions. Step 3: Apply facing direction carefully. Step 4: Verify neighbor-based clues.

sections.title: Single Variable (Color/Fruit Preference)
sections.content: Each person may like a different color or fruit. After fixing seating positions, create a separate column for the variable. Use elimination method to assign preferences correctly without violating any clue.

sections.title: Handling Multiple Possibilities
sections.content: Sometimes one clue creates two possible cases. Draw two separate diagrams and continue solving both. As more clues are applied, one case will violate a condition and can be eliminated.

sections.title: 3-4 Step Solution Strategy
sections.content: Step 1: Identify structure (double row, circle, square). Step 2: Apply strong or fixed clues first. Step 3: Mark facing direction and apply position clues carefully. Step 4: Add variable information and eliminate incorrect possibilities.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Forgetting opposite position logic in double rows. 2. Confusing left-right in mixed circular cases. 3. Not maintaining separate cases. 4. Assigning variables too early without confirmation.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 requires structured diagram drawing, careful direction handling, and elimination method. Always verify opposite positions and variable assignments before finalizing the answer.

tricks.title: Opposite Column Rule
tricks.explanation: In double rows, opposite persons are always in the same column.
tricks.example: If A sits third from left in Row 1, the person opposite A is also third from left in Row 2.

tricks.title: Mark Facing Direction Clearly
tricks.explanation: Always write N, S, C, or O beside names.
tricks.example: A (C), B (O) helps avoid left-right confusion.

tricks.title: Corner First Strategy
tricks.explanation: In square arrangements, fill corner positions first.
tricks.example: If C sits at a corner, place C in one of four corner boxes.

tricks.title: Two-Case Method
tricks.explanation: If two arrangements are possible, draw both.
tricks.example: A may sit left or right of B, so test both separately.

tricks.title: Variable After Seating
tricks.explanation: Fix seating positions before assigning colors or fruits.
tricks.example: Once A’s seat is fixed, then assign Red or Apple.

tricks.title: Neighbor Counting Trick
tricks.explanation: Corner persons have fewer neighbors than side-middle persons.
tricks.example: If a person has exactly two neighbors, likely at a corner.

tricks.title: Cross-Verification Rule
tricks.explanation: After each new clue, recheck the full arrangement.
tricks.example: Ensure opposite and left-right clues still match.

tricks.title: Row Labeling Method
tricks.explanation: Name rows as Row 1 and Row 2 for clarity.

tricks.title: Eliminate Immediately
tricks.explanation: If any case violates one clue, remove it instantly.
tricks.example: If A cannot sit at extreme, discard that case.

tricks.title: Slow Position Counting
tricks.explanation: Count seats carefully in circular cases.
tricks.example: Second to right means count two positions only.
